questions.q: Why is the earth called a connected system?
questions.a: Its air, water, land and life constantly exchange matter and energy - change in one affects all.

questions.q: Give one example of interaction between spheres.
questions.a: Volcanoes (lithosphere) throw ash into the atmosphere, cooling climate and affecting seas and life.

questions.q: Why study the earth as one system?
questions.a: Problems like climate change cut across spheres, so solutions must consider everything together.

concepts.title: Cycles of Matter: Water, Carbon and Nutrients

questions.q: Name three cycles of matter in nature.
questions.a: Water cycle, carbon cycle and nitrogen cycle (also oxygen cycle).

questions.q: What keeps the water cycle running?
questions.a: Solar energy evaporating water, which condenses to clouds and returns as rain and snow.

questions.q: Why is the nitrogen cycle essential for life?
questions.a: It converts air's nitrogen into soil nitrates that plants need to build proteins.

questions.q: How does energy enter an ecosystem?
questions.a: As sunlight captured by green plants in photosynthesis.

questions.q: State the ten per cent law of energy flow.
questions.a: Only about 10% of energy passes from one trophic level to the next; the rest is lost as heat.

questions.q: Why are decomposers the recycling agents of an ecosystem?
questions.a: They break dead matter into soil nutrients that producers reuse, completing the loop.
